_doc: THE single table of what on a NucleoOS SD card belongs to the DEVICE / the USER, read at runtime by every
tool that writes a card: deploy.ps1 (staging + -To), sd-sync.ps1, push-ota.mjs, sd-net-sync.mjs and
tools/nucleo-sd-deploy/sd_deploy.py (update/provision/verify and the release payload). A path classified
as device state is never staged, shipped, pushed or overwritten by any of them.
isDeviceState(path): true if it matches a 'state' pattern; otherwise, under data/anima/ it is state unless
it matches an 'animaShip' pattern (the ANIMA brain + firmware-pinned seeds ship; the API key, learned
caches, profile, sessions... are the user's, and new ANIMA state files are protected automatically).
Patterns: SD-relative, case-insensitive (FAT). '*' = any characters except '/', '**' = any characters
including '/' ('**/' also matches nothing), nothing else is special. Implementations: tools/lib/
sd-policy.mjs, sd_deploy.py, deploy.ps1 / sd-sync.ps1 — all held to tools/lib/sd-policy-vectors.json by
tools/sd-policy.test.mjs. The firmware's delete guard (nucleo_fsprotect.h) and the factory-reset lists
(app_wifi.cpp) answer different questions and are not generated from this file.
_media: data/ROMs, data/DOS, data/Music, data/Videos are user media too, but NOT listed as state: push-ota --include-media deliberately ships them (bundled factory games, dev media). Tools skip them unless asked.
